conviction_note: The whole event is one binary -- whether the 07:00 RNS repeats 'Adjusted earnings per share in line with current market expectations' against the 202.8p FY26 consensus the company itself published on 23 July, because H1 (38-42p) is already pre-announced and carries no news. The arithmetic behind that sentence is extreme and unreported (H2 must be ~4x H1, an 80/20 split against 51/49 in 2025) which is why the finding sum is -1.8; but the issuer has now gone 61 days without a Regulatory RNS while publishing its own consensus, and September interims are the one slot this company has never used to warn (2024-09-19 -4.27%, 2025-09-18 +1.91%), so my scenario tree (65% reaffirm +2.5, 25% soften -11, 10% upbeat +8) gives about -0.3. I emit -1.0: visibly smaller in magnitude than the -1.8 sum because the +2.295 positioning lean opposes me and 111,234 shares of disclosed short is 13.9 sessions of median volume, which is real squeeze fuel on any reaffirmation. print_vs_bar and expected_move differ because the H1 number will land inside its pre-announced range while the outlook language is where I expect the slippage, and a slipped outlook on a stock 2.7% off a 52-week low is only worth so much.
bar: FY2026 adjusted basic EPS of 202.8p and FY2027 of 231.4p, both stated by the company as 'current consensus market expectations' in footnotes to its own 23 July 2026 RNS; H1 2026 adjusted EPS pre-announced at 38p-42p in the same RNS. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/half-year-trading-update-and-notice-of-results/9682935 (2026-07-23)

positioning_check: Disclosed net short 1.67% of shares outstanding at position date 17/08/2026, down from 2.19% (FCA aggregated register as read by the sealed baseline, as_of 2026-09-19, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). Covering, not building -- but stale: the register has not moved for five weeks while the stock fell a further 3.8%. Holder detail from the FCA per-holder file (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx, downloaded 2026-09-22) and Investegate's mirror (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/JDG/short-positions) shows ONE dominant seller, GLG Partners LP, which peaked at 1.82% on 2026-02-11 and then filed 1.78% (24-Mar), 1.68% (16-Apr), 1.58% (27-Apr), 1.47% (08-May), 1.36% (19-May) -- a seven-month monotonic wind-down into a 41% price fall, i.e. profit-taking, not a forced buy-in. findings.finding: The company's own 23 July RNS pre-announces H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p and, in a footnote, puts FY2026 consensus at 202.8p -- so the 'in line' the market is holding requires roughly 162p of H2 adjusted EPS, about four times H1 and an ~80/20 split, against 141.4p/133.9p (51/49) in 2025; the same RNS reports the order book at 17.3 weeks, which reads as improvement only against the FY25 year-end 15.7 but is flat against the like-for-like H1 2025 comparator of 17.4 weeks printed in the same sentence, and on a sales base 21% lower is roughly 21% smaller in absolute terms, with order intake down 11%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Judges has downgraded or disappointed at three of its last five scheduled statements and the stock moved -11.61% (Trading Update 2024-11-18), -15.19% (Half Year Trading Update 2025-07-24) and about -11% (Full Year Trading Statement 2026-01-22, Proactive) on those days -- so when this line surprises on this name it surprises double-digit and the UK tail is not truncated. But the two September interims in the observed RNS history moved only -4.27% (2024-09-19) and +1.91% (2025-09-18), because the July trading update had already carried the half-year news both times; and the 2026-07-23 update itself, which contained the 38-42p, the -21% revenue and the Geotek slip to 2028, moved the stock only -1.62% (4625.0 -> 4550.0, Yahoo daily closes) and it closed higher the next day.
findings.original_quote: adjusted earnings per share in the first half is expected to be in the range of 38p-42p ... The order book was 17.3 weeks (FY 2025: 15.7 weeks; H1 2025: 17.4 weeks). ... Across the Group, order intake was down 11% compared with H1 2025 ... * Current consensus market expectations for the year ended 31 December 2026 are Adjusted basic earnings per share of 202.8p.
findings.why_not_priced: The 202.8p footnote and the 38-42p are both public, but no source I could reach does the division. Every piece of secondary coverage I found reported the flattering order-book comparator (Sharecast/Halifax and the Stockopedia brief both frame it as '17.3 weeks compared with 15.7 weeks at the end of 2025') and none states the implied H2 EPS or the 80/20 split. This is a 4-analyst, GBP 250m AIM name trading about USD 446k a day, so the marginal price-setter is a retail or adviser reader of exactly that wire summary. If the arithmetic were priced you would not see all four published targets sitting above spot (average 6450p, Berenberg buy 5600p reiterated 25 July 2026, and even Jefferies' underperform target of 4015p is 7% above the 3750p spot) and you would not see the whole 19% de-rating since 23 July happen on a median 8,030 shares a day with no analyst revision in between.
findings.independence: Separately corroborated as a fact pattern by the company's 22 January 2026 statement, which guided FY2026 to 200-250p explicitly 'assuming no rebound in US demand and no contribution from Geotek's next coring expedition' -- and the July RNS then pushed that expedition from early 2027 to 'no earlier than 2028', so the FY26 bar has not moved while the 2027 support under it has been removed: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/judges-scientific-says-starts-2026-with-lower-than-desired-order-book-ce7e58d2de8ff725 (2026-01-22). Note this finding deliberately merges what were two sizes in my pre-local draft (the H2 arithmetic and the order-book framing) because both rest on the same RNS document.

findings.finding: The Investegate regulated-news record shows Judges has filed nothing price-sensitive in the 61 days since it reaffirmed FY2026 -- only a Notice of Investor Presentation (12 Aug) and two Share Incentive Plan PDMR notices (6 Aug, 10 Sep) -- from an issuer that publishes its own consensus number and has a demonstrated habit of putting bad news out in a standalone RNS, which under MAR Article 17 makes two months of silence evidence the board does not presently believe 202.8p is materially unachievable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three times this board concluded it would miss, it said so in a dedicated RNS and the stock fell double digits the same morning (2024-11-18 -11.61%, 2025-07-24 -15.19%, 2026-01-22 about -11%). The two times it reached September interims without having warned first, the reaction was -4.27% (2024) and +1.91% (2025). So the informative event for this name has historically been the warning RNS, not the results RNS.
findings.original_quote: 10 Sep 2026 04:44 PM RNS Director/PDMR Shareholding | 12 Aug 2026 07:00 AM RNS Notice of Investor Presentation | 06 Aug 2026 05:38 PM RNS Director/PDMR Shareholding | 23 Jul 2026 07:00 AM RNS Half Year Trading Update and Notice of Results
findings.why_not_priced: An absence is not a headline and no aggregator emits it; you can only establish it from a complete domestic RNS mirror, which is what Investegate is. The price is behaving as if a warning were coming -- the stock is at 3750p, 2.7% off its 52-week low of 3650p and 41% below the 6360p high, having fallen 19% from 4625p on 22 July -- but it got there on a median 8,030 shares a day (about GBP 300k), which is a thin tape with no bid rather than a market verdict. If the market had weighed the silence you would expect the drift to have stopped or reversed as the 30-day closed period began around 24 August; instead the stock made new lows on 16, 17, 21 and 22 September. Deliberately sized small and its band crosses zero, because this board has never issued a truly out-of-cycle warning -- it uses its scheduled January and July statements -- and 23 September is itself a scheduled slot it could use.
findings.independence: The six PDMR notices since July are all automatic Share Incentive Plan or dividend-reinvestment purchases of 6 to 8 shares each at 4450.0p (05/08/2026) and 4175.0p (07/09/2026), so nothing in the insider record contradicts or corroborates the silence in either direction -- there is no discretionary director buying at the low either: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/director-pdmr-shareholding/9766456 (2026-09-10).

findings.finding: The bullish half of the baseline's positioning lean is stale and belongs to one manager's profit-taking: the FCA per-holder record shows GLG Partners LP peaked at 1.82% on 2026-02-11 and filed a monotonic 1.78 / 1.68 / 1.58 / 1.47 / 1.36 through 19 May 2026 while the stock fell 41%, and the aggregate has sat at 1.67% since position date 17/08/2026 with no filing in the five weeks since, during which the stock fell another 3.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on this name for a short-covering reaction. What the record does show is that the covering flow has not supported the price at any point: GLG cut from 1.82% to 1.36% between February and May 2026 and the stock fell from roughly 6000p to 4500p over the same stretch, and it cut again into mid-August while the stock fell from 4550p to 3900p.

findings.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline read only the aggregated register, which shows one number and one change (1.67%, -0.52pp) and scores it as `short_building` +1.040 -- a bullish component worth nearly half the +2.295 lean. The per-holder history, which only the FCA's own per-holder file and Investegate's mirror of it carry, shows that change is the tail of a seven-month orderly reduction by a single manager into a 41% decline, and that it stopped five weeks before the print. I am NOT claiming the other half of the lean back: 111,234 shares against 8,030 a day is 13.9 sessions to cover and that squeeze constraint is real, but it is already what `short_squeeze` +1.002 is paying for and I will not double-count it. So this finding is only the correction to the stale component.
findings.independence: The FCA's own per-holder file gives the identical series from a different file to Investegate's page and confirms the mirror is not a rendering artefact -- 56 JDG rows, last dated 2026-05-19: https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx (downloaded 2026-09-22, max position date in file 2026-07-09).

findings.finding: Judges has a written dividend policy of 'increasing dividends by no less than 10% per annum', which implies a 36.0p interim on 23 September against pre-announced H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p -- cover of about 1.1x, against 4.3x on the 32.7p paid a year ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line has never surprised: the company raised the interim 10% to 32.7p in 2025 and the final 10% to 82.3p at the 31 March 2026 prelims -- a day the stock rose 4.48% on results that the same release called disappointing, with the dividend increase the headline positive most coverage led with.
findings.original_quote: In accordance with the Company's policy of increasing dividends by no less than 10% per annum, the Board is declaring an interim dividend of 32.7p (2024: 29.7p), which will be paid on Friday 7 November 2025 ... The interim dividend is covered 4.3 times by Adjusted earnings
findings.why_not_priced: The four analysts will model +10% and the increase itself is not news; what is not modelled anywhere I could reach is that policy compliance now costs the board almost all of first-half earnings, so the declaration is a costly signal rather than a formality and the market is not positioned to read it as one with the stock at a 52-week low. Sized small and with a band that reaches -2.0 because the downside case -- the first break of a policy this company has honoured every year since 2008 -- would be read as a pre-emptive admission about the second half. If the market were pricing that risk the stock would not be holding a roughly 18.5x multiple on the 202.8p consensus.
findings.independence: The facility terms in the same document make a forced cut unlikely and therefore cap this finding's downside: 'GBP 90m RCF alongside a GBP 50m uncommitted accordion facility ... The facilities mature on 1 July 2028 ... Covenants are (1) gearing no greater than three times Adjusted EBITDA; and (2) interest cover no less than three times', with adjusted net debt of GBP 45.7m and gearing of 1.5 times at 30 June 2025 -- https://www.judges.uk.com/__assets__/WebPages/00075/Judges-Scientific-plc-Interim-Report-30-June-2025.pdf

outside_window.finding: The next Geotek coring expedition moved from 'early 2027' (stated 22 January 2026) to 'no earlier than 2028' (stated 23 July 2026), and the company says FY2027 consensus of 231.4p already contains no coring revenue -- so the 2027 number has lost its optionality and will be re-tested at the January 2027 full-year trading statement, not on 23 September.

FY2026 as a whole -- the 202.8p the whole thesis hangs on -- is settled by the full-year trading statement in the second half of January 2027, which is the slot this board has twice used to downgrade (22 January 2026, about -11%).

baseline_tension: It cuts against the lean and is orthogonal to the run-up: the +2.295 lean is almost entirely a positioning read (short_squeeze +1.002, short_building +1.040) and my strongest finding says the short_building half is a five-week-stale reading of one manager's profit-taking, while my fundamental finding on the guide is negative -- so I am arguing against the largest lean in today's run, which is why the emitted -1.0 is visibly shrunk from the -1.8 finding sum; the -5.06% 20-day run-up, meanwhile, understates the real de-rating (-19% since 22 July) but was produced on a median 8,030 shares a day and is close to meaningless as a market verdict on this name.
local_pass_note: Added the MAR-silence finding (+1.3, the largest single change to the number): only a complete domestic RNS mirror establishes that nothing price-sensitive has been filed since 23 July, and that flipped my central case from 'a downgrade is coming' to 'the modal outcome is a reaffirmation'. expected_move moved from -1.5 to -0.9 on this alone before LESSONS.

Re-sized the positioning finding from -0.7 to -0.6 and rewrote its basis: Investegate's per-company short-positions page and the FCA per-holder file named the seller (GLG Partners LP, peak 1.82% on 2026-02-11, monotonic to 1.36% by 19-May-2026) where the English pass only had the aggregate's -0.52pp, and the 1 June 2026 Total Voting Rights RNS gave the 6,660,695 share count that turns 1.67% into 111,234 shares and 13.9 sessions to cover -- which is the one part of the lean I now think is understated rather than overstated.

Added an order-book finding at -0.7 on the like-for-like 17.3 vs 17.4 weeks comparator, after the domestic secondary coverage (Sharecast/Halifax, the Stockopedia brief, HL) all turned out to carry the flattering 15.7-week comparator instead. Checked and discarded three domestic leads: no TR-1 in 14 months, the unexplained 169,718-share day on 2026-08-26, and the FTSE AIM UK 50 September review. All three are in searched_and_found_nothing at zero.
lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding' -- merged the order-book finding (-0.7) into the H2-arithmetic finding, since both are lines of the 23 July RNS. Five findings became four and the merged size is -2.8 rather than -2.0 and -0.7 side by side.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' -- my pre-lessons positioning finding was +0.5, which was mostly me re-stating the lean's own squeeze component after discovering the 13.9-day cover. Flipped to -0.6, keeping only the part that CORRECTS the baseline (the stale short_building component) and explicitly disclaiming the squeeze half as already paid for by short_squeeze +1.002.

'The tail is intact, so do not size as if it were not' -- widened every band. The guidance finding now runs -9.0 to +1.5 rather than -6.5 to +1.0, which is the right shape for a name that has printed -15.19% and -11.61% days inside two years with no UK price limit to truncate them.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' -- raised the guidance finding's point estimate and moved the emitted number from -0.9 to -1.0 rather than letting the lean-shrink rule drag it to the -0.3 my scenario tree gives.

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series; macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis' -- confirmed the decision to carry the US appropriations and China import-tax-exemption angles at zero rather than as a positive on the H2 bridge, and moved them explicitly into searched_and_found_nothing.
'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' -- baseline_tension now states the shrink and its size (from a -1.8 sum to a -1.0 emitted number) instead of noting the tension and emitting the sum.
